result.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
result.summary: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. Crucially, alignment to the guide network cannot transfer learned features, never receives gradients, and does not use labels. We demonstrate that this cross-architecture transfer of "fate" benefits the target network in two key domains: (1) instilling the optimization benefits of depth into shallow networks by aligning them to deeper networks, and (2) transferring representational granularity by using fine-resolution networks to shape the geometry of networks with coarser representations. In both cases, the alignment results in improved downstream performance of the target network. Ultimately, this demonstrates that a model's architectural destiny can be decoupled from its physical structure and explicitly modified at initialization.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把随机初始化网络形成的「初始几何」视为优化先验，提出在训练前将目标网络的表示几何对齐到一个完全不同的随机初始化引导网络，并证明这种跨架构对齐可以把深层网络的深度收益与细粒度表示迁移给浅层或粗粒度目标网络，从而提升下游性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 与视觉推理无直接关联，但其「用无标签、无梯度的引导表示几何塑造目标网络内部状态」的思路，可供核查是否能用于塑造 latent 推理工作区、注入深度或表示粒度等结构性收益。
